subject: Mayor Breanna Lungo-Koehn Re-election Platform
overview: Mayor Breanna Lungo-Koehn presented her reelection platform, summarizing administration accomplishments in municipal charter reform, school planning, and environmental sustainability. The candidate highlighted upcoming housing developments in Medford Square and discussed efforts to address the city's infrastructure backlog.

items.title: Reelection Announcement
items.summary: Mayor Breanna Lungo-Koehn announced her candidacy for reelection, citing a record of leadership grounded in transparency and equity.

items.title: Charter Reform
items.summary: The Mayor advocated for a "yes" vote on the modernized city charter appearing on the November ballot, noting it has not been updated in four decades.

items.title: School Infrastructure and Funding
items.summary: The administration reported progress on the new Medford High School project following the selection of a design architect and discussed the impact of the school funding override.

items.title: Sustainability and Waste Management
items.summary: The city's curbside composting program was highlighted for diverting over 2 million pounds of waste, earning a regional award for environmental stewardship.

items.title: Housing and Economic Development
items.summary: Plans were presented for a mixed-use development in Medford Square and broader zoning efforts to add 1,300 housing units across the city.

items.title: Public Spaces and Infrastructure
items.summary: The Mayor reviewed recent park upgrades and the ongoing challenge of addressing backlogs in street, sidewalk, and water infrastructure repairs.

items.title: Equity and Social Support
items.summary: The candidate emphasized the administration's progress on equity goals and the importance of supporting Medford's most vulnerable residents.

items.title: Closing and Election Reminders
items.summary: The Mayor concluded by requesting support for her reelection and the charter review measure on the November 4th ballot.
